verdict.statement: THE REPAIR IS REAL, IT IS MINIMAL, IT ADJUDICATES NOTHING, AND NOTHING WAS SMUGGLED. I wrote my own resolver from $.derivation.resolutionAlgorithm alone and reproduced resolvedValue.sha256 = 6b4e8b829aec65e91152900f45a38b588a5bc35b361c08aa53749c23fdd09231 EXACTLY on the first run, over the full three-step chain of 26 + 27 + 13 operations with every 'from' guard satisfied under type-exact equality testing bool BEFORE int, zero refusals and zero add-target collisions. I then enumerated every leaf path of the resolved v3 value and of the resolved v4 value and diffed them: 0 removals, 16 leaves changed in place, 162 leaves added, and every one of the 178 positions is accounted for by exactly one of the 13 declared operations. No leaf moved anywhere else. The verdict counts are unmoved at 3 assessed / 1 discharged / 1 not discharged / 1 partially discharged, $.requiredResolutionAssessment[2].status is byte-identical at 'NOT DISCHARGED', and the question of whether retention-tiers.v23 Part B discharges item 3 is left open in terms. The new grade is strictly weaker than the one it replaces. Every published figure I could recompute, I recomputed, and every one reproduced: all four sweep lanes at every published population, all fourteen pinned digests and byte counts, the leaf census in ten categories, the keyLocator in BOTH directions at all 25 top-level keys with zero divergence either way, the flat consuming gate at all six subject positions, both retained resolvers, all four destroyed-pin recoverability classifications against the git recovery point, RT23-B-RES-01 on live D9 bytes, the binding packet's re-extracted content, all seven graded word-numeral cardinality claims, and all thirteen markdown quotations under freeze section 7.7's three-way search. I found no figure in this artifact that is false. My two observations are about the reach of one lane's predicate and about a disclosed inherited key; neither moves the verdict.
